title: bunkr / Off-grid messaging
text: When the network goes down, bunkr keeps useful information moving. This prototype connects two phones through a five-node software mesh.

title: 01 / Send a tiny preview
text: Richard sends a photo of a trail junction. Instead of pushing the entire original, bunkr sends a tiny preview across three radio hops.

title: 02 / Choose what matters
text: Maya receives the image, but the sign is blurry. She opens the preview and selects just the sign: the detail she actually needs.

title: 03 / Request source detail
text: One tap sends a compact request back through the mesh. The sender crops the original photo, and the requested detail takes priority.

title: 04 / Watch detail arrive
text: Verified tiles arrive piece by piece, bringing the sign into focus while the rest stays blurry. This is real source detail, with no AI reconstruction.

title: Useful information. Fewer bytes.
text: Bunkr also supports text and compressed voice notes. The simulator exposes routes, packet loss, retries, and radio settings. Receipt confirmation requires a return acknowledgment. The goal: spend scarce bandwidth on the information that matters.
